title: Column symmetry check
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Suppose $\sigma.n-\sigma.w=dd$, every field of the register state $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2\le B$, $\sigma.u<\sigma.n$, and $\sigma.w\le\sigma.n$. If the encoded adjacency relation is symmetric between row $\sigma.u$ and every column $w'$ with $\sigma.w\le w'<\sigma.n$, then for all $p,a,b\le B$, the program at state $yn$ with $w$ reset to $\sigma.n$ and $p,a,b$ set to those values has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If this column-symmetry condition does not hold, then $q=0$ and the program at state $y2$ with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
hypotheses_covered: Every field of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
If the stated symmetry condition holds, then for every $p,a,b\le B$ the specified state-$yn$ configuration has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$
If the symmetry condition fails, then $q=0$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and $dd$ a
natural number. Suppose the register record $\sigma$ satisfies $\sigma.n-\sigma.w=dd$,
every register is at most $B$, $2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2\le B$, $\sigma.u<\sigma.n$, and
$\sigma.w\le\sigma.n$. If the encoded adjacency relation is symmetric for every column
$w'$ from $\sigma.w$ up to but not including $\sigma.n$ in row $\sigma.u$, then for all
$p,a,b\le B$, the program at state $yn$ with $w$ reset to $\sigma.n$ and $p,a,b$ set to
those values has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If that
column-symmetry condition fails, then $q=0$ implies the program at state $y2$ with
record $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
